routes.label: Rule out three cubes and build with four

question:
A figure is constructed from unit cubes. Each cube shares at least one face with another cube. What is the minimum number of cubes needed to build a figure with the front and side views shown?

[Figure 1](figures/2003_AMC_8_Q15_question_fig1.svg)
solution:
Each view contains three unit squares, so at least three cubes are needed. To determine whether three can work, first locate the upper cube.

The front view fixes its position across the figure, and the side view fixes its position in depth. Together these restrictions allow exactly one cube in the upper level. There can be no cube beside it at that level or above it, so the face-sharing condition forces a cube directly beneath it.

Suppose there were only three cubes. After making this two-cube stack, only one cube would remain. To produce the other bottom square in the front view, this cube must be displaced from the stack across the figure. To produce the other bottom square in the side view, it must also be displaced in depth. It would therefore sit diagonally from the bottom of the stack and share no face with either stacked cube. This violates the condition, so three cubes cannot work.

Four cubes do work: place three bottom cubes in an L and put the fourth cube above the L’s corner. Orient the L so the stack appears on the left in the front view and on the right in the side view. The two arms supply the remaining bottom squares in the respective views. Each arm cube and the upper cube share a face with the corner cube.

Thus the minimum is \(\boxed{4}\) cubes, choice \(\mathrm{B}\).
